profile.name: Mike Croley
profile.bio: Mike Croley is a former park ranger and the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 6th Congressional District in 2026. No further public biographical information was confirmed.
profile.notes: The campaign website did not load during research, so no platform could be recorded; occupation comes from Tennessee Lookout coverage cited on Wikipedia.

profile.name: Darden Copeland
profile.bio: Darden Copeland is a consultant and business owner who presents himself as a first-time candidate from a working-class background whose only elected role has been church elder. He ran in the Democratic primary for the 2025 special election in Tennessee's 7th District and is the 2026 Democratic nominee.

platform.point: Wants to protect Medicaid, keep premiums affordable, lower prescription drug prices and keep rural hospitals open.
Supports a full congressional stock-trading ban, term limits and refusing corporate PAC money.
Opposes benefit cuts, privatization or raising the retirement age.
Targets housing, grocery and childcare costs through price-gouging oversight and making corporations pay their fair share.
Pledges to act as an independent check on any president rather than a rubber stamp.

economy.evidence: Wants corporations and the wealthy to pay a fair share and supports price-gouging oversight.

welfare.evidence: Opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security and supports lower drug costs.

profile.name: Brent Taylor
profile.bio: Brent Taylor has represented District 31 in the Tennessee Senate since 2023. He served 12 years on the Memphis City Council starting in 1995 and later on the Shelby County Commission and election commission. He is a funeral director who co-founded a family-owned funeral business in the Memphis area.

platform.point: Makes crime reduction in Shelby County his central focus, including work with the Memphis Safe Task Force.
Backs a state constitutional amendment to deny bail for the most serious violent crimes.
Campaigns on making Memphis matter in Washington.
Says he supports President Trump's agenda.
Says he has repeatedly defended the constitutional right to bear arms.
Highlights that he never voted for a tax increase on the city council and backs small-business legislation.

economy.evidence: Says he never voted to raise taxes and has supported business-friendly legislation.

security.evidence: Sponsored juvenile-crime bills and backed a state constitutional amendment to deny bail for major violent crimes.

profile.notes: Economy score is newly added from his campaign biography; other positions beyond crime are thinly documented.

profile.name: Angela Rodriguez Prilliman
profile.bio: Angela "Heli" Rodriguez Prilliman is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 12th congressional district and lives in Fort Worth. She grew up in Stephenville and graduated from Texas A&M University. She has more than ten years of experience in the technology sector as an entrepreneur and educator.

platform.point: Calls for universal health care coverage.
Supports universal access to child care.
Pledges to fully fund public schools.
Says she will work to protect voting rights.
Wants to reduce the influence of billionaire money in politics.

welfare.evidence: Campaigns for universal health care and universal child care.

education.evidence: Pledges to fully fund public schools.

profile.name: Adam Bauman
profile.current_role: Canine drug-detection business owner and former Border Patrol agent
profile.bio: Adam Bauman is the Republican nominee for Texas's 16th congressional district, having won the May 2026 primary runoff. He is a U.S. Navy veteran who served as a Special Warfare Combatant Crewman and a former U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Border Patrol Tactical Team. He came to El Paso with Border Patrol in 2001 and now runs a canine drug-detection business.

platform.point: Calls for a secure border to curb crime and drug trafficking in El Paso.
Wants to work with local leaders to lower El Paso property taxes.
Pledges to speed up veterans' benefits and expand job training.
Opposes raising the retirement age and wants changes to keep the program solvent past 2034.
Seeks lower insurance premiums without additional federal subsidies.
Supports women-only sports competitions and facilities.

liberty.evidence: Supports women-only sports and facilities (LGBTQ); no stated positions found on abortion, drugs, guns or speech.

immigration.evidence: Backs Customs and Border Protection operations to secure the border against crime and drug trafficking.

profile.notes: Liberty and immigration scores are new and rest on a few campaign statements. His welfare views are mixed: he opposes raising the Social Security age and also opposes more federal insurance subsidies.

profile.name: Casey Shepard
profile.bio: Casey Shepard is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 17th congressional district. A Central Texas native who grew up near Waco, he holds a bachelor's degree from Loyola Marymount University and a law degree from the UC Davis School of Law. He practices indigent criminal defense in Waco.

platform.point: Wants stronger congressional oversight of the executive branch and protection of judicial independence.
Proposes fully funding SNAP and school meals and restoring international food aid.
Restore support for Medicaid and Medicare and widen the medical workforce, including trained immigrant professionals.
Supports tax incentives for affordable housing, full rental assistance funding and ending tariffs on building materials.
Supports abolishing ICE and updating immigration rules for trained medical and construction workers.

welfare.evidence: Calls for fully funded SNAP and school meals, full rental assistance and restored Medicaid and Medicare support.

liberty.evidence: Supports protecting abortion rights (abortion); no stated positions found on other liberty issues.

immigration.evidence: Supports abolishing ICE and immigration reform to admit more medical and construction workers.

profile.notes: All scores are new, based on his campaign site and debate coverage. During the primary he said he had previously voted in Republican primaries because his county lacked Democratic contests.

profile.name: Ronald Whitfield
profile.bio: Ronald Whitfield is a landscaping contractor and the Republican nominee for Texas's 18th congressional district. He also ran for the seat in the 2025–26 special election.
profile.notes: No campaign website or public issue positions were found; Ballotpedia was unreachable during research.

profile.name: Marquette Greene-Scott
profile.bio: Marquette Greene-Scott is a city council member and mayor pro tem in Iowa Colony, Texas, and a former teacher who moved to Texas from Louisiana in 2010. She was the Democratic nominee for this district in 2024.

platform.point: Pass universal healthcare and protect the Affordable Care Act.
Fund the VA fully, strengthen oversight and expand mental health support for military families.
Pair more border security resources and faster case processing with a path to citizenship for people brought as children.
Protect voting rights, end partisan gerrymandering and tighten campaign finance rules.
Restore abortion rights after the overturning of Roe v. Wade.

welfare.evidence: Calls for universal healthcare not tied to employment.

liberty.evidence: Supports restoring abortion rights after Roe v. Wade was overturned.

immigration.evidence: Supports a path to citizenship alongside increased border security resources.

profile.notes: Liberty score reflects only her abortion position, as other liberty issues were not found.
